title: Dōgen (Eihei Dōgen)
summary: Dōgen, dated 1200 to 1253, is described by a Concise Oxford dictionary entry as the founder of the Sōtō Zen school in Japan. After studying in China he returned in 1227 and taught shikantaza, or just sitting. In 1244 he founded Eihei-ji temple in present-day Fukui Prefecture, which remains one of the school's two head temples.

uncertainty.note: Sources disagree on the death year: one gives 1253, the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy gives 1254 in its 1200–54 range. Dates of birth and death are given as years only.
